headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Planning Your Master Bathroom Renovation
articleBody:
Renovating a master bathroom is an exciting investment, but simple missteps during early planning can create costly delays. Planning carefully around your daily routine keeps the project running smoothly.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Demolishing before ordering finishes: Ripping out tile before vanity sets, plumbing trim, and custom tiles are delivered leaves your bathroom unusable if unexpected supply delays pop up.
- Ignoring hidden water damage: Assuming wall studs and subfloors are pristine can blow your timeline; always keep contingency room for unexpected leak repairs.
- Shifting plumbing locations late: Deciding to move a toilet or relocate drain stacks after rough-in work has started triggers expensive rework and new permit inspections.
- Underestimating ventilation needs: Skimping on the exhaust fan creates chronic humidity that degrades paint, cabinets, and drywall over time.
- Skipping written scopes and allowances: Moving forward without clear specifications on fixtures, permits, and payment milestones makes costs harder to control.

Working with an experienced contractor ensures hidden issues are resolved before new materials go in.
